verses.original: Κατήντησεν δὲ καὶ εἰς Δέρβην καὶ εἰς Λύστραν καὶ ἰδοὺ μαθητής τις ἦν ἐκεῖ ὀνόματι Τιμόθεος υἱὸς γυναικὸς Ἰουδαίας πιστῆς πατρὸς δὲ Ἕλληνος
verses.transliteration: Katēntēsen de kai eis Derbēn kai eis Lystran kai idou mathētēs tis ēn ekei onomati Timotheos huios gynaikos Ioudaias pistēs patros de Hellēnos
verses.literal: Paul came to Derbe and then to Lystra where he found a disciple named Timothy the son of a believing Jewish woman and a Greek father

verses.original: ὃς ἐμαρτυρεῖτο ὑπὸ τῶν ἐν Λύστροις καὶ Ἰκονίῳ ἀδελφῶν
verses.transliteration: hos emartyreito hypo tōn en Lystrois kai Ikoniō adelphōn
verses.literal: The brothers in Lystra and Iconium spoke well of him

verses.original: τοῦτον ἠθέλησεν ὁ Παῦλος σὺν αὐτῷ ἐξελθεῖν καὶ λαβὼν περιέτεμεν αὐτὸν διὰ τοὺς Ἰουδαίους τοὺς ὄντας ἐν τοῖς τόποις ἐκείνοις ᾔδεισαν γὰρ ἅπαντες ὅτι Ἕλλην ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ ὑπῆρχεν
verses.transliteration: touton ēthelēsen ho Paulos syn autō exelthein kai labōn perietemen auton dia tous Ioudaious tous ontas en tois topois ekeinois ēdeisan gar hapantes hoti Hellēn ho patēr autou hypērchen
verses.literal: Paul wanted Timothy to accompany . . . him so he took him and circumcised him on account of the Jews - in that area for they all knew that his father was a Greek

verses.original: Ὡς δὲ διεπορεύοντο τὰς πόλεις παρεδίδοσαν αὐτοῖς φυλάσσειν τὰ δόγματα τὰ κεκριμένα ὑπὸ τῶν ἀποστόλων καὶ πρεσβυτέρων τῶν ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις
verses.transliteration: Hōs de dieporeuonto tas poleis paredidosan autois phylassein ta dogmata ta kekrimena hypo tōn apostolōn kai presbyterōn tōn en Hierosolymois
verses.literal: As they went from town to town they delivered the decisions handed down by the apostles and elders in Jerusalem for the people to obey

verses.original: Αἱ μὲν οὖν ἐκκλησίαι ἐστερεοῦντο τῇ πίστει καὶ ἐπερίσσευον τῷ ἀριθμῷ καθ’ ἡμέραν
verses.transliteration: Hai men oun ekklēsiai estereounto tē pistei kai eperisseuon tō arithmō kath’ hēmeran
verses.literal: So the churches were strengthened in the faith and grew daily in numbers

verses.original: Διῆλθον δὲ τὴν Φρυγίαν καὶ Γαλατικὴν χώραν κωλυθέντες ὑπὸ τοῦ Ἁγίου Πνεύματος λαλῆσαι τὸν λόγον ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ
verses.transliteration: Diēlthon de tēn Phrygian kai Galatikēn chōran kōlythentes hypo tou Hagiou Pneumatos lalēsai ton logon en tē Asia
verses.literal: After the Holy Spirit had prevented them from speaking the word in the province of Asia they traveled through the region of Phrygia and Galatia

verses.original: ἐλθόντες δὲ κατὰ τὴν Μυσίαν ἐπείραζον εἰς τὴν Βιθυνίαν πορευθῆναι καὶ οὐκ εἴασεν αὐτοὺς τὸ Πνεῦμα Ἰησοῦ
verses.transliteration: elthontes de kata tēn Mysian epeirazon eis tēn Bithynian poreuthēnai kai ouk eiasen autous to Pneuma Iēsou
verses.literal: And when they came to the border of Mysia they tried to enter . . . Bithynia but the Spirit of Jesus would not permit them

verses.original: παρελθόντες δὲ τὴν Μυσίαν κατέβησαν εἰς Τρῳάδα
verses.transliteration: parelthontes de tēn Mysian katebēsan eis Trōada
verses.literal: So they passed by Mysia and went down to Troas

verses.original: Καὶ ὅραμα διὰ τῆς νυκτὸς τῷ Παύλῳ ὤφθη ἀνὴρ Μακεδών τις ἦν ἑστὼς καὶ παρακαλῶν αὐτὸν καὶ λέγων Διαβὰς εἰς Μακεδονίαν βοήθησον ἡμῖν
verses.transliteration: Kai horama dia tēs nyktos tō Paulō ōphthē anēr Makedōn tis ēn hestōs kai parakalōn auton kai legōn Diabas eis Makedonian boēthēson hēmin
verses.literal: During the night Paul had a vision of a man of Macedonia standing and pleading with him - Come over to Macedonia and help us

verses.original: ὡς δὲ τὸ ὅραμα εἶδεν εὐθέως ἐζητήσαμεν ἐξελθεῖν εἰς Μακεδονίαν συμβιβάζοντες ὅτι προσκέκληται ἡμᾶς ὁ Θεὸς εὐαγγελίσασθαι αὐτούς
verses.transliteration: hōs de to horama eiden eutheōs ezētēsamen exelthein eis Makedonian symbibazontes hoti proskeklētai hēmas ho Theos euangelisasthai autous
verses.literal: As soon as Paul had seen the vision we got ready to leave for Macedonia concluding that God had called us to preach the gospel to them

verses.original: Ἀναχθέντες δὲ ἀπὸ Τρῳάδος εὐθυδρομήσαμεν εἰς Σαμοθρᾴκην τῇ δὲ ἐπιούσῃ εἰς Νέαν Πόλιν
verses.transliteration: Anachthentes de apo Trōados euthydromēsamen eis Samothrakēn tē de epiousē eis Nean Polin
verses.literal: We sailed from Troas straight to Samothrace and the following day on to Neapolis . . .

verses.original: κἀκεῖθεν εἰς Φιλίππους ἥτις ἐστὶν πρώτη τῆς μερίδος Μακεδονίας πόλις κολωνία Ἦμεν δὲ ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ πόλει διατρίβοντες ἡμέρας τινάς
verses.transliteration: kakeithen eis Philippous hētis estin prōtē tēs meridos Makedonias polis kolōnia Ēmen de en tautē tē polei diatribontes hēmeras tinas
verses.literal: From there we went to the Roman colony of Philippi - the leading city of that district of Macedonia And we stayed there several days

verses.original: Τῇ τε ἡμέρᾳ τῶν σαββάτων ἐξήλθομεν ἔξω τῆς πύλης παρὰ ποταμὸν οὗ ἐνομίζομεν προσευχὴν εἶναι καὶ καθίσαντες ἐλαλοῦμεν ταῖς συνελθούσαις γυναιξίν
verses.transliteration: Tē te hēmera tōn sabbatōn exēlthomen exō tēs pylēs para potamon hou enomizomen proseuchēn einai kai kathisantes elaloumen tais synelthousais gynaixin
verses.literal: On the Sabbath . . . we went outside the city gate along the river where it was customary to find a place of prayer After sitting down we spoke to the women who had gathered there

verses.original: Καί τις γυνὴ ὀνόματι Λυδία πορφυρόπωλις πόλεως Θυατείρων σεβομένη τὸν Θεόν ἤκουεν ἧς ὁ Κύριος διήνοιξεν τὴν καρδίαν προσέχειν τοῖς λαλουμένοις ὑπὸ τοῦ Παύλου
verses.transliteration: Kai tis gynē onomati Lydia porphyropōlis poleōs Thyateirōn sebomenē ton Theon ēkouen hēs ho Kyrios diēnoixen tēn kardian prosechein tois laloumenois hypo tou Paulou
verses.literal: Among those listening was a woman named Lydia a dealer in purple cloth from the city of Thyatira who was a worshiper of God The Lord opened her heart to respond to - Paul’s message

verses.original: ὡς δὲ ἐβαπτίσθη καὶ ὁ οἶκος αὐτῆς παρεκάλεσεν λέγουσα Εἰ κεκρίκατέ με πιστὴν τῷ Κυρίῳ εἶναι εἰσελθόντες εἰς τὸν οἶκόν μου μένετε καὶ παρεβιάσατο ἡμᾶς
verses.transliteration: hōs de ebaptisthē kai ho oikos autēs parekalesen legousa Ei kekrikate me pistēn tō Kyriō einai eiselthontes eis ton oikon mou menete kai parebiasato hēmas
verses.literal: And when she and her household had been baptized she urged us . . . If you consider me a believer in the Lord come and stay at my house And she persuaded us

verses.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ πορευομένων ἡμῶν εἰς τὴν προσευχὴν παιδίσκην τινὰ ἔχουσαν πνεῦμα Πύθωνα ὑπαντῆσαι ἡμῖν ἥτις ἐργασίαν πολλὴν παρεῖχεν τοῖς κυρίοις αὐτῆς μαντευομένη
verses.transliteration: Egeneto de poreuomenōn hēmōn eis tēn proseuchēn paidiskēn tina echousan pneuma Pythōna hypantēsai hēmin hētis ergasian pollēn pareichen tois kyriois autēs manteuomenē
verses.literal: One day . . . as we were going to the place of prayer we were met by a slave girl with a spirit of divination who earned a large income for her masters by fortune-telling

verses.original: αὕτη κατακολουθοῦσα τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ ἡμῖν ἔκραζεν λέγουσα Οὗτοι οἱ ἄνθρωποι δοῦλοι τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ Ὑψίστου εἰσίν οἵτινες καταγγέλλουσιν ὑμῖν ὁδὸν σωτηρίας
verses.transliteration: hautē katakolouthousa tō Paulō kai hēmin ekrazen legousa Houtoi hoi anthrōpoi douloi tou Theou tou Hypsistou eisin hoitines katangellousin hymin hodon sōtērias
verses.literal: This girl followed Paul and the rest of us shouting . . . These men are servants of the Most High God who are proclaiming to you the way of salvation

verses.original: Τοῦτο δὲ ἐποίει ἐπὶ πολλὰς ἡμέρας διαπονηθεὶς δὲ Παῦλος καὶ ἐπιστρέψας τῷ πνεύματι εἶπεν Παραγγέλλω σοι ἐν ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐξελθεῖν ἀπ’ αὐτῆς καὶ ἐξῆλθεν αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ
verses.transliteration: Touto de epoiei epi pollas hēmeras diaponētheis de Paulos kai epistrepsas tō pneumati eipen Parangellō soi en onomati Iēsou Christou exelthein ap’ autēs kai exēlthen autē tē hōra
verses.literal: She continued this for many days Eventually Paul grew so aggravated that he turned and said to the spirit In the name of Jesus Christ I command you to come out of her And the spirit left her at that very moment

verses.original: Ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ κύριοι αὐτῆς ὅτι ἐξῆλθεν ἡ ἐλπὶς τῆς ἐργασίας αὐτῶν ἐπιλαβόμενοι τὸν Παῦλον καὶ τὸν Σιλᾶν εἵλκυσαν εἰς τὴν ἀγορὰν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἄρχοντας
verses.transliteration: Idontes de hoi kyrioi autēs hoti exēlthen hē elpis tēs ergasias autōn epilabomenoi ton Paulon kai ton Silan heilkysan eis tēn agoran epi tous archontas
verses.literal: When the girl’s owners saw that their hope of making money was gone they seized Paul and Silas and dragged them before the authorities in the marketplace

verses.original: καὶ προσαγαγόντες αὐτοὺς τοῖς στρατηγοῖς εἶπαν Οὗτοι οἱ ἄνθρωποι ἐκταράσσουσιν ἡμῶν τὴν πόλιν Ἰουδαῖοι ὑπάρχοντες
verses.transliteration: kai prosagagontes autous tois stratēgois eipan Houtoi hoi anthrōpoi ektarassousin hēmōn tēn polin Ioudaioi hyparchontes
verses.literal: They brought them . . . to the magistrates and said These men are Jews and are throwing our city into turmoil

verses.original: καὶ καταγγέλλουσιν ἔθη ἃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν ἡμῖν παραδέχεσθαι οὐδὲ ποιεῖν Ῥωμαίοις οὖσιν
verses.transliteration: kai katangellousin ethē ha ouk exestin hēmin paradechesthai oude poiein Rhōmaiois ousin
verses.literal: by promoting customs that are unlawful for us Romans to adopt or practice

verses.original: Καὶ συνεπέστη ὁ ὄχλος κατ’ αὐτῶν καὶ οἱ στρατηγοὶ περιρήξαντες αὐτῶν τὰ ἱμάτια ἐκέλευον ῥαβδίζειν
verses.transliteration: Kai synepestē ho ochlos kat’ autōn kai hoi stratēgoi perirēxantes autōn ta himatia ekeleuon rhabdizein
verses.literal: The crowd joined in the attack against Paul and Silas and the magistrates ordered that they be stripped . . . . . . . . . and beaten with rods

verses.original: πολλάς τε ἐπιθέντες αὐτοῖς πληγὰς ἔβαλον εἰς φυλακήν παραγγείλαντες τῷ δεσμοφύλακι ἀσφαλῶς τηρεῖν αὐτούς
verses.transliteration: pollas te epithentes autois plēgas ebalon eis phylakēn parangeilantes tō desmophylaki asphalōs tērein autous
verses.literal: And after striking them with many blows they threw them into prison and ordered the jailer to guard them securely

verses.original: ὃς παραγγελίαν τοιαύτην λαβὼν ἔβαλεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν ἐσωτέραν φυλακὴν καὶ τοὺς πόδας ἠσφαλίσατο αὐτῶν εἰς τὸ ξύλον
verses.transliteration: hos parangelian toiautēn labōn ebalen autous eis tēn esōteran phylakēn kai tous podas ēsphalisato autōn eis to xylon
verses.literal: On receiving this order he placed them in the inner cell and fastened their feet in the stocks

verses.original: Κατὰ δὲ τὸ μεσονύκτιον Παῦλος καὶ Σιλᾶς προσευχόμενοι ὕμνουν τὸν Θεόν ἐπηκροῶντο δὲ αὐτῶν οἱ δέσμιοι
verses.transliteration: Kata de to mesonyktion Paulos kai Silas proseuchomenoi hymnoun ton Theon epēkroōnto de autōn hoi desmioi
verses.literal: About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God and the other prisoners were listening to them

verses.original: ἄφνω δὲ σεισμὸς ἐγένετο μέγας ὥστε σαλευθῆναι τὰ θεμέλια τοῦ δεσμωτηρίου ἠνεῴχθησαν δὲ παραχρῆμα αἱ θύραι πᾶσαι καὶ πάντων τὰ δεσμὰ ἀνέθη
verses.transliteration: aphnō de seismos egeneto megas hōste saleuthēnai ta themelia tou desmōtēriou ēneōchthēsan de parachrēma hai thyrai pasai kai pantōn ta desma anethē
verses.literal: Suddenly a strong earthquake shook the foundations of the prison At once all the doors flew open and everyone’s chains came loose

verses.original: Ἔξυπνος δὲ γενόμενος ὁ δεσμοφύλαξ καὶ ἰδὼν ἀνεῳγμένας τὰς θύρας τῆς φυλακῆς σπασάμενος τὴν μάχαιραν ἤμελλεν ἑαυτὸν ἀναιρεῖν νομίζων ἐκπεφευγέναι τοὺς δεσμίους
verses.transliteration: Exypnos de genomenos ho desmophylax kai idōn aneōgmenas tas thyras tēs phylakēs spasamenos tēn machairan ēmellen heauton anairein nomizōn ekpepheugenai tous desmious
verses.literal: When the jailer woke up and saw the prison doors open he drew his sword and was about to kill himself presuming that the prisoners had escaped

verses.original: ἐφώνησεν δὲ ὁ Παῦλος μεγάλῃ φωνῇ λέγων Μηδὲν πράξῃς σεαυτῷ κακόν ἅπαντες γάρ ἐσμεν ἐνθάδε
verses.transliteration: ephōnēsen de ho Paulos megalē phōnē legōn Mēden praxēs seautō kakon hapantes gar esmen enthade
verses.literal: But Paul called out in a loud voice Do not harm yourself We are all here

verses.original: Αἰτήσας δὲ φῶτα εἰσεπήδησεν καὶ ἔντρομος γενόμενος προσέπεσεν τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ τῷ Σιλᾷ
verses.transliteration: Aitēsas de phōta eisepēdēsen kai entromos genomenos prosepesen tō Paulō kai tō Sila
verses.literal: Calling for lights the jailer rushed in and fell trembling before Paul and Silas

verses.original: καὶ προαγαγὼν αὐτοὺς ἔξω ἔφη Κύριοι τί με δεῖ ποιεῖν ἵνα σωθῶ
verses.transliteration: kai proagagōn autous exō ephē Kyrioi ti me dei poiein hina sōthō
verses.literal: Then he brought them out and asked Sirs what must I do to be saved

verses.original: Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν Πίστευσον ἐπὶ τὸν Κύριον Ἰησοῦν καὶ σωθήσῃ σὺ καὶ ὁ οἶκός σου
verses.transliteration: Hoi de eipan Pisteuson epi ton Kyrion Iēsoun kai sōthēsē sy kai ho oikos sou
verses.literal: They replied Believe in the Lord Jesus and you will be saved you and your household

verses.original: καὶ ἐλάλησαν αὐτῷ τὸν λόγον τοῦ κυρίου σὺν πᾶσιν τοῖς ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: kai elalēsan autō ton logon tou kyriou syn pasin tois en tē oikia autou
verses.literal: Then Paul and Silas spoke the word of the Lord to him and to everyone . . . in his house

verses.original: καὶ παραλαβὼν αὐτοὺς ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ τῆς νυκτὸς ἔλουσεν ἀπὸ τῶν πληγῶν καὶ ἐβαπτίσθη αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ αὐτοῦ πάντες παραχρῆμα
verses.transliteration: kai paralabōn autous en ekeinē tē hōra tēs nyktos elousen apo tōn plēgōn kai ebaptisthē autos kai hoi autou pantes parachrēma
verses.literal: At that hour of the night the jailer took them and washed their wounds And without delay he and all his household were baptized

verses.original: ἀναγαγών τε αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν οἶκον παρέθηκεν τράπεζαν καὶ ἠγαλλιάσατο πανοικεὶ πεπιστευκὼς τῷ Θεῷ
verses.transliteration: anagagōn te autous eis ton oikon parethēken trapezan kai ēgalliasato panoikei pepisteukōs tō Theō
verses.literal: Then he brought them into his home and set a meal before them So he and all his household rejoiced that they had come to believe in God

verses.original: Ἡμέρας δὲ γενομένης ἀπέστειλαν οἱ στρατηγοὶ τοὺς ῥαβδούχους λέγοντες Ἀπόλυσον τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἐκείνους
verses.transliteration: Hēmeras de genomenēs apesteilan hoi stratēgoi tous rhabdouchous legontes Apolyson tous anthrōpous ekeinous
verses.literal: When daylight came the magistrates sent their officers with the order Release those men

verses.original: Ἀπήγγειλεν δὲ ὁ δεσμοφύλαξ τοὺς λόγους τούτους πρὸς τὸν Παῦλον ὅτι Ἀπέσταλκαν οἱ στρατηγοὶ ἵνα ἀπολυθῆτε νῦν οὖν ἐξελθόντες πορεύεσθε ἐν εἰρήνῃ
verses.transliteration: Apēngeilen de ho desmophylax tous logous toutous pros ton Paulon hoti Apestalkan hoi stratēgoi hina apolythēte nyn oun exelthontes poreuesthe en eirēnē
verses.literal: The jailer informed . . . . . . . . . . . . Paul The magistrates have sent orders to release you Now you may go on your way in peace

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ Παῦλος ἔφη πρὸς αὐτούς Δείραντες ἡμᾶς δημοσίᾳ ἀκατακρίτους ἀνθρώπους Ῥωμαίους ὑπάρχοντας ἔβαλαν εἰς φυλακήν καὶ νῦν λάθρᾳ ἡμᾶς ἐκβάλλουσιν οὐ γάρ ἀλλὰ ἐλθόντες αὐτοὶ ἡμᾶς ἐξαγαγέτωσαν
verses.transliteration: Ho de Paulos ephē pros autous Deirantes hēmas dēmosia akatakritous anthrōpous Rhōmaious hyparchontas ebalan eis phylakēn kai nyn lathra hēmas ekballousin ou gar alla elthontes autoi hēmas exagagetōsan
verses.literal: But Paul said to the officers They beat us publicly without a trial . . . and threw us into prison even though we are Roman citizens And now do they want to send us away . . . secretly Absolutely not . . . . . . Let them come themselves and escort us out . . .

verses.original: Ἀπήγγειλαν δὲ τοῖς στρατηγοῖς οἱ ῥαβδοῦχοι τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα ἐφοβήθησαν δὲ ἀκούσαντες ὅτι Ῥωμαῖοί εἰσιν
verses.transliteration: Apēngeilan de tois stratēgois hoi rhabdouchoi ta rhēmata tauta ephobēthēsan de akousantes hoti Rhōmaioi eisin
verses.literal: So the officers relayed this message to the magistrates who were alarmed to hear that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens

verses.original: καὶ ἐλθόντες παρεκάλεσαν αὐτούς καὶ ἐξαγαγόντες ἠρώτων ἀπελθεῖν ἀπὸ τῆς πόλεως
verses.transliteration: kai elthontes parekalesan autous kai exagagontes ērōtōn apelthein apo tēs poleōs
verses.literal: They came to appease them and led them out requesting that they leave . . . the city

verses.original: ἐξελθόντες δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς φυλακῆς εἰσῆλθον πρὸς τὴν Λυδίαν καὶ ἰδόντες παρεκάλεσαν τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς καὶ ἐξῆλθαν
verses.transliteration: exelthontes de apo tēs phylakēs eisēlthon pros tēn Lydian kai idontes parekalesan tous adelphous kai exēlthan
verses.literal: After Paul and Silas came out of the prison they went to Lydia’s house to see the brothers and encourage them Then they left the city
